newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on peso, FOMC hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on peso, FOMC hopes.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates eased 10 basis points to close at 21.40 percent on Wednesday on a stable peso and a calmer outlook for U.S. interest rates, traders said.
"The (March 25) Federal Open Market Committee meeting is well discounted by now, no changes in base rates are expected," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour contracts had earlier closed 0.5 centavos softer at 7.9350/7.9400 due to pre-weekend swaps rather than fundamental weakness, traders said.
Cetes overnight rates traded between a relatively narrow range of between 21.10 and 21.50 percent, traders said.
Dealers said the session had been quiet as Wednesday saw the cutoff date for banks settling outstanding balances on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 40 basis points at 23.10 percent.
Banco de Mxico drained 833 million from the market, or slightly less than usual due to demand for liquidity ahead of the central bank's cutoff, traders said.
Total liquidity of 9.454 billion pesos was expected to return to the market on Thursday from previous central bank operations, traders said.
Thursday also sees the central bank place government securities it auctioned on Tuesday night, but total maturities would exceed new issues by 784 million pesos and thus cut into market liquidity.
Dealers estimated corporations would also pay tax bills amounting to some nine billion pesos, which would squeeze liquidity further.
